A.explanation: Moving backwards would increase the anticlockwise moment of the 600 N passenger and add to the anticlockwise moment from the 90 N force, so balance would be lost.

B.explanation: A 60 mm forward shift reduces the passenger anticlockwise moment by $600 \times 0.060 = 36 \text{ N m}$, which exactly cancels the $90 \times 0.400 = 36 \text{ N m}$ anticlockwise moment of the driving force about the axle.

C.explanation: 140 mm is the new distance of the passenger behind the axle after moving 60 mm forwards from 200 mm behind, not the distance moved.

D.explanation: 140 mm forwards confuses the final position with the change in position and gives a weight moment change of $600 \times 0.140 = 84 \text{ N m}$, much larger than the $36 \text{ N m}$ needed.

hints: Take moments about the axle: the 600 N machine acts 200 mm in front and the 600 N passenger acts 200 mm behind, so their weight moments cancel when stationary.
The 90 N horizontal force acts at the ground, which is one wheel radius of 400 mm below the axle, so its moment about the axle is $90 \text{ N} \times 400 \text{ mm}$.

Decide whether that driving-force moment is clockwise or anticlockwise, then decide which way the 600 N passenger must shift to supply an equal opposite moment and calculate $600 \text{ N} \times \Delta x$.
walkthrough: Take moments about the axle for balance. Clockwise is taken as positive. Stationary: machine moment $= +600 \text{ N} \times 200 \text{ mm}$ and passenger moment $= -600 \text{ N} \times 200 \text{ mm}$, so net moment is zero.

When driving forwards, the 90 N horizontal force at the ground has perpendicular distance equal to the wheel radius, $400 \text{ mm}$, below the axle. Its moment is $M = Fd = 90 \times 400 = 36000 \text{ N mm} = 36 \text{ N m}$.
The ground contact is below the axle and the force is forwards, so this moment is anticlockwise and tends to tip the vehicle backwards. An extra clockwise moment of $36 \text{ N m}$ is needed.
Let the passenger move $\Delta x$ forwards. Moving forwards reduces his anticlockwise moment. Change in moment $= 600 \text{ N} \times \Delta x$ clockwise.

For balance: $600 \times \Delta x = 90 \times 0.400$. So $600 \times \Delta x = 36$, giving $\Delta x = 0.060 \text{ m} = 60 \text{ mm}$ forwards. His new position is still $140 \text{ mm}$ behind the axle. This is option B.
